items.title: Create SM Context can fail when PCF association is slow or unreachable
items.description:
PDU Session Update SM Context can fail on AMF with:

```bash
[amf_sbi] [error] Could not find Nsmf_PDUSession URI
```

That is a consequence of a failed Create.

Issue:

1. AMF sends Create SM Context to SMF
2. With `use_local_pcc_rules: no`, SMF tries to associate with PCF before answering Create.
3. The SMF HTTP API waits up to `FUTURE_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS` (100 ms)(`SMContextsCollectionApiImpl.cpp`) -\> this is blocking, no response = no SM Context creation

If the PCF HTTP call takes longer than 100 ms (it was reported with a WSL2 setup), Create returns error 504 without `Location` (which is needed for the SM context). A later Update then fails because AMF cannot build the context to modify.

Usually, if the PCF connect finishes under 100 ms (e.g. native Linux), SMF still completes Create, returns `Location`, falls back to default rules when PCF association fails, and Update works.

Some ideas about the solution:

1. should the PCF association be blocking for the SM context creation? if not, Create SM Context should complete with a fallback regardless
2. HTTP timeout vs FUTURE_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS -\> are they aligned or maybe HTTP can take longer than 100s ? why not wait for the full HTTP timeout?

items.title: SUPI should be stored as string
items.description:
In the current SMF UE Context implementation, the SUPI is stored inside the supi64_t(uint64_t) in many occasion and it is also used as key for the smfcontext map. However, the conversion from string to uint64_t may cause issues when using the test plmn (001/01) since the two leftest zeros of the IMSI are lost.
Indeed, even if most of the smf procedures seem to be not impacted, service exposure is impacted. 

An example, with PDU Session Establishment callback (SUPI is 101000000001 instead of 00101000000001) 
` {"adIpv4Addr":"12.1.0.2","dnn":"oai","event":"PDU_SES_EST","pduSeId":1,"pduSessType":"IPV4","snssai":{"sd":"FFFFFF","sst":1},"supi":"101000000001","timeStamp":3934429717}`

items.title: [Proposal] Use new NGAP lib from common src
PFCP Modification Request Scenarios
items.description:
Noticed that the Modification request is not updating `QERs` but instead creating new ones. Indeed, within the `PFCP Establishment request`; two `QERs` with `IDs` ( `1` and `2`, respectively) (i.e., `QER# 1`, `QER# 2`, respectively), which correspond to `GBR` and `NON-GBR` traffic, respectively.  For `QER# 1`, the `MBR_DL` and `GBR_DL` are set to 0. Therefore, it is supposed to update these values within the `PFCP Modification Request` . However, in the `PFCP Modification Request` it is noticed that, instead of sending `Update QER` , new `Add QER` was created with ID `3` and `4` , ( `QER# 3` for `GBR` and `QER# 4` for `NON-GBR`). This time, the `MBR_DL` and `GBR_DL` for `QER# 3`  are non null, while the `MBR_UL` and `GBR_UL`  are null.

What can be noticed here is that `QER# 1` and even `QER# 3`  are not updated and wont be updated. Therefore, `QER#1` is never used.

attached a pcap capture for the scenario.

[capture-smf-qos-proof-of-concept.pcap](/uploads/ae053cf75da386055cfbf10533a5e24d/capture-smf-qos-proof-of-concept.pcap)

items.title: Wrong qos_data profile
items.description:
the SMF/PCF is not checking the QoS profiles that are used withing the config file.

As an example the one onboarded withing the fed repository:

```
$ cat oai-cn5g-fed/docker-compose/policies/qos/qos_data

 non-gbr-qos-5qi-9:
  5qi: 9
  arp:
    priorityLevel: 15
    preemptCap: NOT_PREEMPT
    preemptVuln: PREEMPTABLE
  priorityLevel: 10

 gbr-qos-5qi-1:
  5qi: 1
  maxbrUl: 70000 Kbps
  maxbrDl: 100 Mbps
  gbrUl: 50 Mbps
  gbrDl: 50 Mbps
  arp:
    priorityLevel: 1
    preemptCap: MAY_PREEMPT
    preemptVuln: NOT_PREEMPTABLE
  priorityLevel: 9

 gbr-qos-5qi-5:
   5qi: 5
   maxbrUl: 60 Mbps
   maxbrDl: 100 Mbps
   gbrUl: 50 Mbps
   gbrDl: 50 Mbps
   arp:
     priorityLevel: 1
     preemptCap: MAY_PREEMPT
     preemptVuln: NOT_PREEMPTABLE
   priorityLevel: 8
```

I do have two concerns here:

1. According to 3GPP, `5qi: 5` is considered as `non-gbr` type of QoS Flow, and in the config file, it is considered as `gbr` 
2. It would be more easy to debug when 5QI and QFI have the same values (this is not an issue, but more a wish)

   ![image (1).png](/uploads/f534b0822beda2a524f155ce514bdca9/image__1_.png)

items.title: NGAP: Wrong S-AMBR
items.description:
# Issue
* I have seen that for NGAP the S-AMBR is calculated wrongly, there are some edge cases where it is not correct. 
* I have fixed the AMBR calculation for NAS and Lukas has fixed the GBR calculation for NGAP

@phine_lukas I suggest you have a look and integrate it into your GBR bitrate fix (The bitrate logic is the same between GBR and AMBR)

I think the problem is in this function in `smf_context.cpp`: 

```
void smf_context::get_session_ambr(
    Ngap_PDUSessionAggregateMaximumBitRate_t& session_ambr,
    const snssai_t& snssai, const std::string& dnn);
```

items.title: Confusing error message when SMF parsing failed
items.description:
# Issue
When the parsing of the `smf` field fails, the error message is quite cryptic and not really userfriendly. for example if we configure the `smf_info` incorrectly (duplicated SNSSAI):
```yaml
  smf_info:
    sNssaiSmfInfoList:
      - sNssai: *embb_slice1
        dnnSmfInfoList:
          - dnn: "oai"
      - sNssai: *embb_slice1
        dnnSmfInfoList:
          - dnn: "ims"
```

We get the following unnecessary error msg:
`[2023-08-28 15:09:59.634] [config ] [warning] Could not parse smf: [json.exception.parse_error.101] parse error at line 1, column 35: syntax error while parsing value - invalid literal; last read: '"sNssai": &'`

items.title: SMF should re-register in case it receives 404 from NRF
items.description:
:exclamation: I did not read what the standards say about this, but I imagine it would be a nice feature:

1) NF (e.g. SMF) has existing NRF connection, sends PATCH heartbeats
2) NRF crashes, loses all it's repository infos
3) NF continues with PATCH heartbeats, NRF sends 404, because it does not have the information
4) NF restarts its NRF registration procedure

items.title: SMF goes into a heartbeattimer busy loop when NRF profile response could not be read
items.description:
# Issue
When NF instance registration response data could not be parsed, or there is an error, this error is not handled correctly (`smf_sbi.cpp` line 483 following (for new HTTP client config)).

This leads to the issue that the heartbeat timer in NF profile is set to 0, which results in a busy loop for the 

# Possible implications
* SMF becomes unusable
* Network may get delayed
* Attacker could intercept these messages and just remove the body, which leads to an SMF "busy loop" 

# Possible Solution
Implement a validation (for these error cases but also for API input in general) to set the heartbeat value to a minimum level (e.g. 5 seconds)

items.title: SMF uses HTTP1 towards UDM
items.description:
# Issue
SMF uses HTTP1 towards UDM, even if HTTP/2 is activated. This behavior is recreated in the new configuration (!202), because the UDM does not reply to the SMF request over HTTP/2.

# Solution
Use HTTP/2 for SMF in `smf_sbi` and fix HTTP/2 issue in UDM for the `sm-data` URL

items.title: Do not resolve DNS names on startup
items.description:
# Issue
When resolving all NFs on startup, we create dependencies on the startup order which are not necessary/unwanted. 

# Solution
We should only resolve NFs when we actually use them. Curl is able to resolve FQDNs, so we should let curl handle it accordingly.

items.title: Feature Request: DNS per DNN name
items.description: I suppose every `dnn` should have a dedicated DNS. We can keep this feature optional and have a default DNS as we have today.

items.title: SMF does not clean up curl header list correctly
items.description:
# Description
For each subsequent HTTP request towards AMF (N1N2 Communication), SMF adds a new `Content-Type` header, resulting in larger and larger HTTP requests (and memory consumption)

# Consequence
At some point AMF (after 578 requests) does not accept the request anymore (413), see also [smf_issue_headers_get_long.pcapng](/uploads/242b7fd4bb2006ebc90b1a349196a429/smf_issue_headers_get_long.pcapng)

items.title: SMF does not send a proper response to PDU Session Establishment when IP pool is full
items.description:
# Description
When the SMF does not have any IPs left in the IP pool for a DNN, it does not indicate an error message towards AMF.
Instead, it sends a 408 HTTP code and the AMF does not send an attach reject to the UE. 

# Test Steps
* Make the IP pool small (2 IP addresses)
* Attach 3 UEs
* Third UE will not get any response

items.title: SD value in NSSAI not standard-compliant in CN SBI interfaces
items.description:
# Issue
According to TS 29.571 the definition of the SD value in the SNSSAI data type is as follows:
```
3-octet string, representing the Slice Differentiator, in
hexadecimal representation. Each character in the
string shall take a value of "0" to "9", "a" to "f" or "A"
to "F" and shall represent 4 bits. The most significant
character representing the 4 most significant bits of
the SD shall appear first in the string, and the
character representing the 4 least significant bit of
the SD shall appear last in the string.
This is an optional parameter that complements the
Slice/Service type(s) to allow to differentiate
amongst multiple Network Slices of the same
Slice/Service type. This IE shall be absent if no SD
value is associated with the SST.
Pattern: '^[A-Fa-f0-9]{6}$'
```

## Current situation
Currently, we only support decimal values in SMF. MR !159 solves this by expecting "0x" leading the hex value, but this is not standard-compliant. Our CN components take the values configured by the user and puts them 1:1 in the SBI APIs but we should verify the values and send it standard-compliant in the API.

# Solution
We should have standard-compliant SD values over the whole CN, including AMF and UPF. Additionally, NRF should verify the data in its API

items.description:
When the PFCP Session Establishment towards VPP-UPF fails, it adds custom IEs. It seems these are not understood by the PFCP layer, resulting in an exception. This exception is handled in smf_app(), but the answer should be handled in procedure so we can send an error towards AMF (PDU session establishment reject). At the moment, the SMF just does not reply to the AMF. 

The trace is from the feature_upf_selection branch where the SMF sends the wrong IEs. Still, we should support this scenario.

It is also reproducible when the PFCP Association between SMF and UPF has failed before (e.g. temporary network issue)
